newsitem.title: USA: Gibraltar says purchases boosting results.
newsitem.headline: Gibraltar says purchases boosting results.

text.p: Gibraltar Steel said Tuesday that its acquisition plan is expected to help increase 1997 sales by more than $100 million over 1996.
The company said in a statement that 1997 sales are expected to come in between $450 and $475 million. that compares to $343 million in 1996.
Commenting on the company's future, Brian Lipke, chairman and chief executive officer of Gibraltar said, "we continue to feel the impact of the capital expenditures made during 1995-96."

Gibralter said the major capital expenditure for 1997 is the new 56-inch cold-rolled strip mill being installed at its Cleveland facility which is expected to come on line in the fourth quarter. The company expects it to generate annual sales in the $80-85 million range, and reach reach its full capacity within three years.

Mr. Lipke added, "We also see numerous opportunities to build our sales and earnings and expand our heat-treating operations. Our goal is to have annual heat treating revenues of $100 million or more within five years."
Gibralter's Q2 earnings per share of $0.38 versus $0.40 in the same period last year on revenues of $4.3 million.
